messages.subject: why get different phylogenetic tree while reading almost same input file
parts:
Dear Zhian,

I meet two troubles when I try to plot phylogenetic tree. I would like to ask for your favor to have a look. Thank you.

1. When I upload two files in the attachment, they look almost same, just different number of individuals. But I get different layout of Phylogenetic tree. 
    The first file I get below figure:








 











The second file I get below figure:



















I don't know why there is no populations names in the node in the first file, I checked two files, they are almost same. 

2. When I try to get the unrooted plotting, the node labels overlap, I don't know how to avoid? I use the following coding:
   
      plot.phylo(aa1, font = 2, cex = 0.7, adj = 0, tip.color =tipColor, label.offset = 0.04,type=input$rootTree,show.node.label = F,show.tip.label= T)
      
      
      nodelabels(aa1$node.labels, adj = c(1.3, -0.5), frame = "n", cex = 0.7,font = 2, xpd = TRUE)
      
      
      if(input$rootTree!='unrooted'){    
        axisPhylo(3)}

messages.author: d192ec4b1d416345
messages.subject: Re: [poppr] why get different phylogenetic tree while reading almost same input file
parts:
Hello,

1. The reason why you are getting differences in the first two plots is because there is a duplicated label in the poppr_testpostwaregnew.csv file (FR005_17), so poppr is converting those to numeric labels.
2. Plotting a phylogenetic tree without overlapping labels can be difficult, but you should consult the plot.phylo() function and try several of the options: https://www.rdocumentation.org/packages/ape/versions/5.3/topics/plot.phylo I've had some success with it and you can find my code here: https://github.com/everhartlab/brazil-sclerotinia-2017/blob/506828cf312b5fcb952850b8c5093efa4b999c1b/05-Tree.R#L57-L94 I would recommend to use the lab4ut argument.

Best,
Zhian
